- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days) are common; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day averages in early forecast windows; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 7–10 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum; use 1–2 day lag correction for trend continuation.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative, model delays correction; apply early correction (day 2–3) to avoid prolonged overestimation.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until trend stabilizes.
